page: Google Cloud Platform ct5l-hightpu-1t is a specialized accelerator-equipped instance belonging to the TPU Machines family. It features 24 dedicated virtual CPUs on an x86_64 architecture and 48 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The host system is paired with a single Google TPU v5e accelerator equipped with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM for specialized machine learning workloads.

Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of included local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage volumes and appropriate VPC routing for data staging and external connectivity. The 1:2 ratio of host memory to vCPU capacity reflects a compute-dense configuration intended primarily to feed the TPU accelerator rather than caching massive in-memory datasets.

From an architectural standpoint, the inclusion of a single TPU v5e chip delivers dedicated tensor processing capacity without requiring large multi-chip pod allocations. This makes the ct5l-hightpu-1t an effective platform for targeted machine learning tasks, such as mid-sized deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, and specialized numerical computing pipelines optimized for Google Cloud TPU hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform ct5l-hightpu-1t is an accelerator-oriented instance within the TPU Machines family, designed for specialized machine learning and tensor processing workloads. Powered by an x86_64 CPU architecture, it provides 24 dedicated vCPUs and 48 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per core. The compute configuration integrates a single Google TPU v5e chip offering 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance includes no local storage, requiring attached persistent network storage for file systems and data ingestion, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given the dedicated TPU acceleration paired with balanced multi-core host compute, ct5l-hightpu-1t is geared towards model inference, lightweight neural network fine-tuning, and quantitative pipelines adapted for Google TPU environments.
